papers.title: Promising reference genes for RT-qPCR normalization in breast tumors and normal adjacent tissues.
papers.summary: In 20 breast tissue samples (13 tumors, 7 normal adjacent), ten candidate reference genes were ranked via RefFinder (BestKeeper, NormFinder, geNorm, ΔCt). TBP, PUM1, and RER1 were most stable (geomeans 2.21-2.78); traditional housekeeping genes ACTB and GAPDH ranked least stable across all algorithms. Larger-scale validation is required.

papers.title: Silencing with precision: In silico strategies for antisense oligonucleotide engineering.
papers.summary: Review of antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) therapeutics: surveys state-of-the-art in silico tools for ASO design, 3D structural prediction, molecular docking, and simulation, covering their applications and limitations. It argues computational methodologies can improve ASO specificity and efficacy, deepen mechanistic understanding, and open pathways toward targeted therapies in personalized medicine.

papers.title: Comparative evaluation of germ cell-specific promoters identifies robust drivers of transgene expression during mouse spermatogenesis.
papers.summary: Mouse germ cell-specific promoters (LDHC, TEX13C, DAZL) were isolated and tested after testicular electroporation. LDHC drove the strongest germ cell-specific expression, followed by DAZL. As proof of concept, LDHC-driven shRNA downregulated c-kit in mouse testis. These promoters suit studies of spermatogenesis, male fertility, and germ cell-targeted genome editing.

papers.title: Molecular identification and resistance-associated gene profiling of non-tuberculous mycobacteria isolated from bovine clinical samples.
papers.summary: From 193 bovine clinical samples in India, 18 non-tuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) isolates were obtained; M. vaccae predominated (66.7%). Resistance-associated genes were screened: rpoB in 88.9% of isolates, katG (16.7%) and gyrA (5.6%) exclusively in M. vaccae; rpsL never amplified. No hotspot mutations; gyrA substitutions noted. Phenotypic susceptibility testing was not performed.

papers.title: Anti-phage defense systems in bacteria: molecular mechanisms and their role in shaping phage therapy strategies.
papers.summary: Review of bacterial anti-phage defense—receptor blockade, restriction, CRISPR-Cas, and signaling systems (Thoeris, CBASS, toxin-antitoxin)—and phage countermeasures like anti-CRISPRs and engineered phages with anti-defense proteins. It integrates these into a framework for defense-informed phage selection, rational phage engineering, and clinical trial design against multidrug-resistant infections.

papers.title: URB597 attenuates experimental sepsis-associated acute kidney injury with reduced renal inflammation, apoptosis, and TLR4/NF-κB activation.
papers.summary: In cecal ligation/puncture rats, the FAAH inhibitor URB597 (0.3 or 0.6 mg/kg, intraperitoneal) reduced BUN, creatinine, NGAL, TNF-α, IL-1β, and renal histopathological injury versus CLP alone. It lowered renal TLR4, p-NF-κB, p-IκB-α, inflammatory cytokines, and cleaved caspase-3/-8, attenuating sepsis-associated acute kidney injury via reduced TLR4/NF-κB activation.

papers.title: PTBP3 promotes diabetic nephropathy via Smad3-dependent podocyte-mesenchymal transition.
papers.summary: Integrated transcriptomics identified PTBP3, an RNA-binding protein, as elevated in diabetic nephropathy, validated in STZ mice and high-glucose podocytes. Knockdown attenuated proteinuria, creatinine, and BUN, ameliorated glomerular injury and fibrosis, and inhibited podocyte epithelial-mesenchymal transition by binding SMAD3's 3'-UTR, stabilizing its mRNA. Targeting PTBP3 shows therapeutic potential in diabetic nephropathy.

papers.title: Redox regulation of telomerase and telomeres in cancer: a critical appraisal of exposure, causality and molecular directness.
papers.summary: Critical review of redox-telomerase literature in cancer, appraising five propositions along exposure, model, causal test, and molecular directness axes. Best-supported findings (peroxide-driven TERT nuclear export; glutathione depletion/repletion) remain pathway-mediated; no study causally links residue-resolved oxidative TERT modification to altered function. Proposes measurements needed to close causality and translation gaps.

papers.title: Glycolysis in bone remodeling: from energy supply to signaling regulation.
papers.summary: Review arguing glycolysis in bone remodeling functions beyond energy supply: HIF-1α/WNT signals promote glycolysis, while glycolytic enzymes and metabolites (lactate, LDH, PDK) act as a signaling hub regulating osteoblast and osteoclast differentiation. Targeting glycolytic nodes is a promising but preliminary therapeutic direction for bone metabolic diseases, requiring further in vivo and clinical study.

papers.title: Evaluation of 18 S rRNA as an endogenous control in OpenArray(®) plasma RNA qPCR workflows.
papers.summary: Using FIELD-trial plasma RNA on TaqMan OpenArray, 18S rRNA showed stable detection across 789 samples (median Ct 14.5, inter-run CV 3.9%), and its inclusion in pre-amplification did not significantly bias four co-amplified targets. Archived versus newly manufactured primer pools showed a small but significant Ct shift yet remained broadly group-level comparable.

papers.title: Assessment and detection of nucleotide excision repair capability in human cells: a critical review of current functional methods.
papers.summary: Review of functional nucleotide excision repair (NER) assays in human cells: biochemical, cellular, and genome-wide approaches measuring excision products, repair synthesis, reporter recovery, lesion removal, and genome-wide damage mapping. Because each interrogates distinct NER stages, method selection should follow the research question, with complementary readouts for comprehensive assessment. Elevated NER can drive therapy resistance.

papers.title: Lipidome as a ferroptotic rheostat in cholangiocarcinoma: A proposed model and its current evidence base.
papers.summary: Review proposing a "ferroptotic rheostat" in cholangiocarcinoma: the membrane MUFA-PE to PUFA-PE ratio may determine ferroptotic fate, centered on ACSL3-driven MUFA enrichment. The authors explicitly flag it as a hypothesis from a single lipidomic study in four cell lines, contextualize FASN-SCD1, ACLY, and FXR axes plus IDH mutations, and outline redox/spatial lipidomics experiments to test it.
